# qisqa

qisqa is a URL shortener. It turns a long URL into a short link such as
`https://short.example/aB3xK` and redirects everyone who opens the short link
to the long URL. Every link expires. A link can also be *secured*: it stops
working shortly after it is first opened, and programs that only preview
links cannot see where it leads. A link can also ask for a password before
it opens. This file describes the HTTP API that creates, edits and deletes
links.

The examples use `https://short.example` as the address of the service and
`$TOKEN` as the API token. A machine-readable description of the same API is
at `/api/openapi.yaml`.

## Auth

Every request to `/api/links` needs this header, with the token of an
account:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

A missing or wrong token, or the token of a disabled account, is answered
with `401`. A client that keeps sending wrong tokens is blocked for a few
minutes and gets `429` for every request.

Bodies are JSON. A request body is a single JSON object of at most 64 KB.
A field the API does not know is an error (`400`), so a misspelled field name
is reported instead of ignored.

The short domain a link belongs to is chosen with `domain`, never by the
`Host` header of the API request. Without `domain` the account's first
domain is used. A domain that is not one of the account's is refused with
`403`. An account edits and deletes only its own links.

## Create a link

`POST /api/links`

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | yes | The long URL. Starts with `http://` or `https://`; at most 2048 bytes. A host with letters outside ASCII is turned into its ASCII `xn--` form, which is what is stored and returned in `url`. Other spellings of a host, such as an IPv4 address written as one number, and a host name with an empty label, such as `evil.example..`, or with an `xn--` label that is not the ASCII form of a name, such as `xn--evil-.example`, are refused (see Rules). |
| `domain` | no | The short domain to create the link on, one of the account's. Default: the account's first domain. |
| `expires_in` | no | How long the link lives: a duration such as `30m`, `12h` or `10d`. Default: set by the service (10 days unless configured otherwise). |
| `expires_after_open` | no | Makes the link secured. A duration: how long the link keeps working after it is first opened. `"0"` means it works exactly once. |
| `password` | no | Makes the link ask for this password, 4 to 128 bytes, before it opens. Only a salted hash of it is kept. |
| `format` | no | The shape of `short_url`: `https`, `https_www`, `bare` or `www`. Default: set by the service. |

```sh
curl -X POST https://short.example/api/links \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com/articles/2026/11/a-long-title?ref=mail", "expires_in": "10d"}'
```

The answer is a link object, with `201` when the link is new and `200` when
the same request was sent within the last 10 minutes: then the link it made
comes back, so a retry does not make a second link.

```json
{
  "code": "aB3xK",
  "domain": "short.example",
  "short_url": "https://short.example/aB3xK",
  "url": "https://example.com/articles/2026/11/a-long-title?ref=mail",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-23T10:00:00Z",
  "secured": false,
  "password": false,
  "created": true
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `code` | The short code: the path of the short link. Letters and digits, case-sensitive. |
| `domain` | The short domain the link is on. |
| `short_url` | The link to hand out, in the requested `format`. |
| `url` | The long URL the link leads to, its host in ASCII form. |
| `expires_at` | When the link stops working. RFC 3339, UTC. |
| `secured` | `true` for a link created with `expires_after_open`. |
| `password` | `true` for a link created with `password`. The password itself is never returned. |
| `created` | `true` if this request created the link, `false` if the same request sent within the last 10 minutes did. |

## Shorten URLs in a text

`POST /api/links` with `text` instead of `url`. Every URL inside the text is
replaced with a short link, and the new text comes back together with the
links.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | yes | The text, at most 10 KB. |
| `urls` | no | Exactly which URLs to shorten. Without it, every URL found in the text is shortened. |
| `domain`, `expires_in`, `expires_after_open`, `password`, `format` | no | As for a single link; applied to every link of the text. |

```sh
curl -X POST https://short.example/api/links \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Read more: https://example.com/articles/2026/11/a-long-title?ref=mail. Thank you!", "format": "bare"}'
```

The answer is always `200`:

```json
{
  "text": "Read more: short.example/aB3xK. Thank you!",
  "links": [
    {
      "code": "aB3xK",
      "domain": "short.example",
      "short_url": "short.example/aB3xK",
      "url": "https://example.com/articles/2026/11/a-long-title?ref=mail",
      "expires_at": "2026-11-23T10:00:00Z",
      "secured": false,
      "password": false,
      "created": true
    }
  ]
}
```

How URLs are found and replaced:

- Only URLs that start with `http://` or `https://` are found. `example.com/page`
  without a scheme is left alone.
- Punctuation after a URL (`. , ; : ! ? ) ] } " '` and punctuation outside
  ASCII such as `» ” …`) is not part of the URL and stays in the text. A
  closing bracket that matches a bracket opened inside the URL, as in
  `https://example.com/wiki/Go_(language)`, belongs to the URL.
- A URL that already points at one of the service's own short domains, with
  or without `www.`, is never replaced: a short link is not shortened again.
- Without `urls`: a URL that may not be shortened (see Rules), or whose short
  link would not be shorter than the URL itself, stays as it is. That is not
  an error, and such a URL has no entry in `links`.
- With `urls`: exactly the listed URLs are shortened and every occurrence of
  them in the text is replaced, even when the short link is longer. A listed
  URL that may not be shortened is an error (`400`). A listed URL that does
  not occur in the text is still shortened and returned in `links`. An empty
  list shortens nothing.
- A URL that occurs several times is one link.
- `links` is in order of first appearance in the text (with `urls`: in the
  order of that list). It is `[]` when nothing was shortened.
- One request creates at most 20 links; more is an error (`400`) and nothing
  is created.

## Edit a link

`PATCH /api/links/{code}?domain=short.example`

The `domain` query parameter is optional and defaults to the account's
first domain. Send at least one field:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | The new long URL. The code stays the same. |
| `expires_in` | The new lifetime, counted from now, shorter or longer than before. |

```sh
curl -X PATCH "https://short.example/api/links/aB3xK?domain=short.example" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com/articles/2026/12/another-title", "expires_in": "3d"}'
```

The answer is `200` and the link object:

```json
{
  "code": "aB3xK",
  "domain": "short.example",
  "short_url": "https://short.example/aB3xK",
  "url": "https://example.com/articles/2026/12/another-title",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-16T10:00:00Z",
  "secured": false,
  "password": false,
  "created": false
}
```

`404`: there is no such link, or it is another account's. `409`: the link is
secured or has a password (such a link cannot be edited). An expired link
works again once it gets a new `expires_in`.

## Delete a link

`DELETE /api/links/{code}?domain=short.example`

The `domain` query parameter is optional, as for edit.

```sh
curl -X DELETE "https://short.example/api/links/aB3xK?domain=short.example" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

The answer is `204` with no body. The link stops working at once. `404`:
there is no such link, or it is another account's.

## Errors

Every error is a JSON object with one field:

```json
{"error": "expires_in: invalid duration \"10x\" (examples: 30m, 12h, 10d)"}
```

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `400` | The request is wrong, or its URL may not be shortened; `error` says what to fix. |
| `401` | The token is missing or wrong, or its account is disabled. |
| `403` | The domain is not one of the account's, or the account has no domain. |
| `404` | No such link, or no such API endpoint. |
| `409` | The link is secured or has a password, and cannot be edited. |
| `429` | This client is blocked for a few minutes after too many bad requests. |
| `500` | The service failed. Try again later. |

## Rules

- **A retry gets the same link.** The same request (account, domain, URL and
  `expires_in`) sent again within 10 minutes returns the link it made. After
  that, or with another URL, domain or `expires_in`, a new link is made.
- **Codes are never used again.** A code stays its link's, also after the
  link expired or was deleted, so an old link never leads somewhere new,
  unless the operator removes the domain and adds it again, loses the
  service's data, or rolls it back without passing over the codes made
  since.
- **Secured and password links are always new.** A request with
  `expires_after_open` or `password` creates a new code every time, even for
  the same URL. Such a link cannot be edited, only deleted.
- **How a secured link opens.** Opening it in a browser shows a small page
  whose script asks the service for the long URL and then goes there.
  Programs that only fetch the page, such as link-preview bots, neither use
  up the link nor learn the long URL. An unopened secured link still expires
  at `expires_at`.
- **How a password link opens.** Opening it in a browser shows a small page
  with one password field. Its script sends `POST /{code}` with
  `{"password": "..."}`. The answer is `200` with `{"url": "..."}` for the
  right password, `403` with `{"error": "wrong password"}` for a wrong one,
  and `429` while the link is locked. Five wrong passwords in a row lock the
  link for five minutes, and a wrong password counts against the client like
  a code that does not exist. No more of a link's passwords are checked at
  once than could still lock it, and the service checks only a few
  passwords of all links at once: a password sent while that many are
  being checked gets `429` with `Retry-After: 1`, is not counted, and can
  be sent again a second later. Neither the page nor a refused attempt holds
  anything of the long URL. A link with both `password` and
  `expires_after_open` asks for the password first, so only the right
  password uses it up.
- **`format`** decides only how `short_url` is written; every form opens the
  same link:
  - `https`: `https://short.example/aB3xK`
  - `https_www`: `https://www.short.example/aB3xK`
  - `bare`: `short.example/aB3xK`
  - `www`: `www.short.example/aB3xK`
- **Which URLs may be shortened.** The URL starts with `http://` or
  `https://`, is at most 2048 bytes long, does not point at one of the
  service's own short domains and not at a host the operator blocked. A
  host with letters outside ASCII, such as `пример.example`, is accepted
  and comes back in its `xn--` form, `xn--e1afmkfd.example`, the name a
  browser looks up; the rules apply to that form. An IPv4 address is
  written as four numbers, like `192.0.2.1`, never in an IPv6 form.
  Other spellings that a browser reads as another host, such as an IPv4
  address written as one number, and a host name with an empty label,
  such as `evil.example..`, or with an `xn--` label that is not the ASCII
  form of a name, such as `xn--evil-.example`, are refused with `400`.
  For example:
  `{"error": "url: write the address as four numbers, like 192.0.2.1"}`. A
  domain may also be limited to certain target hosts; a URL to any other
  host is refused there.
- **Durations** are a number and a unit: `30s`, `15m`, `12h`, `10d`. The longest is `36500d`.
  `expires_in` must be greater than zero.
